plan.title: District Health Dashboard
plan.subtitle: Comparing key health indicators across districts in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha

panels.title: Total households surveyed
panels.sql: SELECT SUM("Households surveyed") AS n FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha')

panels.title: Average literacy rate (women 15-49)
panels.sql: SELECT AVG("Women age 15-49 years who are literate (%)") AS avg_literacy FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha')

panels.title: Vaccination coverage (children 12-23m)
panels.sql: SELECT AVG("Children age 12-23 months fully vaccinated (%)") AS avg_vaccination FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha')

panels.title: Institutional birth rates by district
panels.sql: SELECT "District", "Institutional births (%)" AS birth_rate FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha') AND "District" != 'State Total' ORDER BY birth_rate DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Stunting rates (children under 5) by district
panels.sql: SELECT "District", "Children under 5 years who are stunted (%)" AS stunting_rate FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha') AND "District" != 'State Total' ORDER BY stunting_rate DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top 10 districts by sanitation coverage
panels.sql: SELECT "District", "Households with improved sanitation facility (%)" AS sanitation_rate FROM "district_health_factsheet" WHERE "State" IN ('Bihar', 'Jharkhand', 'Odisha') AND "District" != 'State Total' ORDER BY sanitation_rate DESC LIMIT 10

plan.narrative: This dashboard compares key health indicators across districts in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha. With {{p1}} households surveyed in total, the average literacy rate for women aged 15-49 stands at {{p2}}%, while vaccination coverage for children aged 12-23 months is at {{p3}}%. Institutional birth rates vary significantly, with some districts achieving rates above 90%, while others remain below 70%. Stunting rates in children under five are particularly concerning in several districts, with the highest rates exceeding 50%. Sanitation coverage shows a similar pattern of disparity, with the top 10 districts achieving rates above 80%, while others fall well below. These variations highlight the need for targeted interventions to address the most critical health challenges in each district.
